[{"picto":"liv_interview","createdAt":"2026-09-08T13:31:04+02:00","text":["Enzo Paleni (Groupama-FDJ United) hinted at a hard battle today: “This is the last chance for riders like me. Tomorrow will be flatter, then there’s the time trial, two mountain stages and the finish. Today’s stage suits me, so I’m going to give it my all. The finish isn’t as tough. There are fewer hills, so we’ll have to beat the peloton in a sprint, with a strong group, a good strategy and careful management throughout the day to try and finish ahead of the peloton. Unfortunately, there’ll be a headwind during the day, which could put the breakaway at a disadvantage, but we’ll see what we can do. “The fatigue is definitely there", the Swiss rider said at the start. "The first week you feel more and more tired but now it’s more stable, sometimes you can recover a bit like yesterday, or with Sunday’s stage that was not too long. Of course we have the heat that makes it not easy, but I still enjoy it and we almost see Granada coming."
"[Marco Brenner’s victory] was an absolutely amazing day for Marco and the team, it gives wings to everybody. We just enjoy the moment, of course we have big ambitions for this week and we want to continue like this, but it gives us a boost."
"It could be [a day for the breakaway] but we need a lot of teams with the same idea. Two or three teams definitely want to have a sprint, but if there is a big fight for the breakaway in the start and a good breakaway, in the third week you never know what can happen. Also with the heat and the first part of the race that is not easy. Let’s see, we hope to not have only a calm stage with a sprint, we hope we will see some action today.""],"title":"Thalmann wanted to "stee some action today", so he made the break","createdAt":"2026-09-08T14:02:57+02:00","id":66302,"_id":"55f67284409e9b8bfbf6e3ae326b978439a445b4204093cfc34613c01bec0113","_bind":"publication_en-2026-16","_origin":"news-2026-16","_updatedAt":1788868977425,"_parent":"stage-2026:dbf7fd7af4eb7895c4d2f9ee4f006d4206974d252b631987bd80a72a5df3fdd6","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:thalmann-wanted-to-stee-some-action-today-so-he-made-the-break","model":"news"},{"title":"8 riders on the move","createdAt":"2026-09-08T13:24:21+02:00","year":2026,"publicationAt":"2026-09-08T13:24:21+02:00","stageType":"VAL","text":["They've opened a small gap at km 7."],"updatedBy":"bvittek","type":"liv","picto":"liv_attack","locale":"en","id":66183,"highlight":false,"createdBy":"bvittek","slug":"8-riders-on-the-move-6","pinned":false,"updatedAt":"2026-09-08T13:24:21+02:00","stage":16,"_id":"118729ce7b2b3fea739e24982814218ce8c6d11e966c4aec15514c21a55b6a08","_bind":"publication_en-2026-16","_origin":"news-2026-16","_updatedAt":1788866661189,"_parent":"stage-2026:dbf7fd7af4eb7895c4d2f9ee4f006d4206974d252b631987bd80a72a5df3fdd6","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:8-riders-on-the-move-6","model":"news"},{"id":66223,"highlight":false,"type":"liv","picto":"liv_breakaway","slug":"5-riders-on-the-move-6","stage":16,"createdBy":"bvittek","updatedAt":"2026-09-08T13:34:07+02:00","pinned":false,"title":"5 riders on the move","year":2026,"createdAt":"2026-09-08T13:33:11+02:00","publicationAt":"2026-09-08T13:33:11+02:00","updatedBy":"bvittek","text":["As the road rises, a handful of attackers manage to open a small gap.

It was the case with Jonas Vingegaard last year.
Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. Primoz Roglic was the last to do it, taking La Roja from Ben O’Connor on stage 19 of La Vuelta 24.
This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.
All in all, the six stages in the final week of La Vuelta 26 add up to:
- 907.8 km of racing
- 13,716 metres of elevation gain
- 270 points for the green jersey
- 53 points for the polka-dot jersey."],"updatedBy":"bvittek","stage":16,"_id":"eeeffecac041d1d267f9fa80fc4ce644098a3440ed6f24878b0e2a205b09adc9","_bind":"publication_en-2026-16","_origin":"news-2026-16","_updatedAt":1788864786955,"_parent":"stage-2026:dbf7fd7af4eb7895c4d2f9ee4f006d4206974d252b631987bd80a72a5df3fdd6","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:a-decisive-final-week","model":"news"},{"type":"liv","highlight":false,"createdBy":"bvittek","title":"The lowest finish of La Vuelta 26","slug":"the-lowest-finish-of-la-vuelta-26","updatedAt":"2026-09-08T14:49:21+02:00","id":66397,"createdAt":"2026-09-08T14:49:21+02:00","pinned":false,"stage":16,"year":2026,"stageType":"VAL","locale":"en","text":["At 8 metres above sea level, the finish in La Rabida is the lowest of La Vuelta 26, slightly below the 10 metres of altitude in Monaco (stage 1), Xeraco (stage 8) and Sevilla (stage 17).

Six stages remain on the way to Granada, with a couple of mountain showdowns, the ITT, and three flatter stages that should see baroudeurs and sprinteurs battle it out for the win. Today is the first of these: the 181.1 km route from Cortegana to La Rabida includes 2,250 metres of elevation gain, but that mostly comes from the rolling terrain in the first half of the stage, ahead of a flat run-in to the finish. There are no categorised climbs.
The neutral start is set at 13:05, the start proper at 13:18 after a 4.6 km parade, and the winners should be crowned at around Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. Primoz Roglic was the last to do it, taking La Roja from Ben O’Connor on stage 19 of La Vuelta 24.
This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.

- 907.8 km of racing
- 13,716 metres of elevation gain
- 270 points for the green jersey

Cortegana and La Rabida make their debut as La Vuelta stage towns*.
The stage is entirely set in the province of Huelva, previously visited by La Vuelta in 1997 and 2022. On the last occasion, stage 17 started from Aracena (km 31.4 on today’s route) and headed to the Monasterio de Tentudia (in the province of Badajoz). The breakaway made it to the finish, with Rigoberto Uran taking victory (3rd place for Jesus Herrada). Primoz Roglic did not start after the crashed in the final in Tomares the day before.

the last 25 editions of La Vuelta (2001 - 2025), the overall leader at the beginning of the second week has won the event on 16 occasions. It was the case with Jonas Vingegaard last year.
Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. Primoz Roglic was the last to do it, taking La Roja from Ben O’Connor on stage 19 of La Vuelta 24.
This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.
All in all, the six stages in the final week of La Vuelta 26 add up to:
- 907.8 km of racing
- 13,716 metres of elevation gain
- 270 points for the green jersey
- 53 points for the polka-dot jersey."],"updatedBy":"bvittek","stage":16,"_id":"eeeffecac041d1d267f9fa80fc4ce644098a3440ed6f24878b0e2a205b09adc9","_bind":"publication_en-2026-16","_origin":"news-2026-16","_updatedAt":1788864786955,"_parent":"stage-2026:dbf7fd7af4eb7895c4d2f9ee4f006d4206974d252b631987bd80a72a5df3fdd6","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:a-decisive-final-week","model":"news"},{"stage":16,"createdAt":"2026-09-08T16:56:38+02:00","slug":"the-6th-sprint-of-la-vuelta-26","stageType":"VAL","type":"liv","picto":"liv_statistics","updatedBy":"bvittek","text":["Stage 2: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) wins in Manosque

This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.

the last 25 editions of La Vuelta (2001 - 2025), the overall leader at the beginning of the second week has won the event on 16 occasions. It was the case with Jonas Vingegaard last year.
Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. Primoz Roglic was the last to do it, taking La Roja from Ben O’Connor on stage 19 of La Vuelta 24.
This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.
All in all, the six stages in the final week of La Vuelta 26 add up to:
- 907.8 km of racing
- 13,716 metres of elevation gain
- 270 points for the green jersey
- 53 points for the polka-dot jersey."],"updatedBy":"bvittek","stage":16,"_id":"eeeffecac041d1d267f9fa80fc4ce644098a3440ed6f24878b0e2a205b09adc9","_bind":"publication_en-2026-16","_origin":"news-2026-16","_updatedAt":1788864786955,"_parent":"stage-2026:dbf7fd7af4eb7895c4d2f9ee4f006d4206974d252b631987bd80a72a5df3fdd6","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:a-decisive-final-week","model":"news"},{"stage":16,"createdAt":"2026-09-08T16:56:38+02:00","slug":"the-6th-sprint-of-la-vuelta-26","stageType":"VAL","type":"liv","picto":"liv_statistics","updatedBy":"bvittek","text":["Stage 2: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) wins in Manosque

This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.

the final week of his first Grand Tour, Roland Thalmann (Tudor) found the strength to make today's breakaway.
“The fatigue is definitely there", the Swiss rider said at the start. "The first week you feel more and more tired but now it’s more stable, sometimes you can recover a bit like yesterday, or with Sunday’s stage that was not too long. Of course we have the heat that makes it not easy, but I still enjoy it and we almost see Granada coming."
"[Marco Brenner’s victory] was an absolutely amazing day for Marco and the team, it gives wings to everybody. We just enjoy the moment, of course we have big ambitions for this week and we want to continue like this, but it gives us a boost."
"It could be [a day for the breakaway] but we need a lot of teams with the same idea. the last 25 editions of La Vuelta (2001 - 2025), the overall leader at the beginning of the second week has won the event on 16 occasions. It was the case with Jonas Vingegaard last year.
Nine editions saw a rider take the lead in the final week and eventually triumph. Primoz Roglic was the last to do it, taking La Roja from Ben O’Connor on stage 19 of La Vuelta 24.
This week offers several opportunities to shake the race, most notably with the individual time trial to Jerez de la Frontera (stage 18) and the two mountains showdowns on days 19 and 20.
All in all, the six stages in the final week of La Vuelta 26 add up to:
- 907.8 km of racing
- 13,716 metres of elevation gain
- 270 points for the green jersey
- 53 points for the polka-dot jersey."],"updatedBy":"bvittek","stage":16,"_id":"eeeffecac041d1d267f9fa80fc4ce644098a3440ed6f24878b0e2a205b09adc9","_bind":"publication_en-2026-16","_origin":"news-2026-16","_updatedAt":1788864786955,"_parent":"stage-2026:dbf7fd7af4eb7895c4d2f9ee4f006d4206974d252b631987bd80a72a5df3fdd6","_key":"_id","_virtual":"news:a-decisive-final-week","model":"news"},{"stage":16,"createdAt":"2026-09-08T16:56:38+02:00","slug":"the-6th-sprint-of-la-vuelta-26","stageType":"VAL","type":"liv","picto":"liv_statistics","updatedBy":"bvittek","text":["Stage 2: Matthew Brennan (Visma-Lease a Bike) wins in Manosque
